description: Nieleze's overarching framework for understanding how organizations detect, interpret, escalate, and act on emerging conditions before visible failure.
The loss or degradation of the connection between emerging signals and timely organizational decisions.
A structural model for examining how emerging conditions move through organizational escalation pathways toward failure or containment.
An assessment of how organizations detect, interpret, escalate, and respond to emerging conditions.
A framework for examining relationships among organizational interpretation, coordination, responsibility, and action.
The clarity with which organizational structures, signals, responsibilities, and decision pathways can be understood under complexity.
A framework concerning governance mechanisms associated with failures of organizational interpretation and the divergence between governance structures and operational reality.
The degradation of an organization's ability to diagnose and respond to emerging governance conditions.
A framework for distinguishing different organizational approaches to sensing emerging conditions and signals.
Mechanisms through which potentially significant signals become weakened, obscured, normalized, absorbed, or prevented from reaching decision-makers.
A framework concerning structural capacity to absorb changing conditions while maintaining effective operation and retaining recovery and adaptation capacity.
The convergence of different oversight weaknesses toward systemic degradation or failure.
A methodology for identifying comparable structural mechanisms across different sectors and domains without treating those domains as equivalent.
